goal_id: arm-ringbuf
version: 1
owner: xiang
intent: >
  Deliver a ring buffer for the sensor ISR of our ARM64 SoC: logically correct,
  builds for aarch64, and meets the ISR latency budget on the real board.
requirements:
  - id: R1
    description: Ring buffer logic is correct (push/pop/full/empty/wrap-around)
    mandatory: true
    predicate: "test_ringbuf passes"
    accept: {methods: [host_unit_test, simulation, real_hardware]}
  - id: R2
    description: Code compiles for the aarch64 target
    mandatory: true
    predicate: "object file is an AArch64 ELF (e_machine=183)"
    accept: {methods: [cross_compile, real_hardware]}
  - id: R3
    description: rb_push+rb_pop stay under 2 microseconds p99 on the real board
    mandatory: true
    hard: true
    predicate: "bench on board reports p99 < 2us"
    accept: {methods: [real_hardware], partial_methods: [simulation]}
checks:
  - id: logic
    proves: [R1]
    alternatives:
      - {id: host-cc, method: host_unit_test, command: "mkdir -p build && cc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror -o build/test_ringbuf tests/test_ringbuf.c src/ringbuf.c && ./build/test_ringbuf", requires: {tools: [cc]}, limitations: "host x86/arm build; proves portable logic only"}
  - id: xbuild
    proves: [R2]
    alternatives:
      - {id: gcc-cross, method: cross_compile, command: "mkdir -p build && aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror -c src/ringbuf.c -o build/ringbuf.aarch64.o && python3 tools/check_elf.py build/ringbuf.aarch64.o aarch64", requires: {tools: [aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc]}}
      - {id: zig-cc, method: cross_compile, command: "mkdir -p build && zig cc -target aarch64-linux-musl -c src/ringbuf.c -o build/ringbuf.aarch64.o && python3 tools/check_elf.py build/ringbuf.aarch64.o aarch64", requires: {tools: [zig]}}
      - {id: clang-target, method: cross_compile, command: "mkdir -p build && clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu -ffreestanding -std=c11 -Wall -Werror -c src/ringbuf.c -o build/ringbuf.aarch64.o && python3 tools/check_elf.py build/ringbuf.aarch64.o aarch64", requires: {tools: [clang]}, limitations: "compile-only (no aarch64 sysroot to link); freestanding code so this covers R2"}
  - id: latency
    proves: [R3]
    alternatives:
      - {id: board-ssh, method: real_hardware, command: "ssh \"$RVD_ARM_BOARD_SSH\" ./bench_ringbuf --p99-max-us 2", requires: {env: [RVD_ARM_BOARD_SSH], tools: [ssh]}, risk: medium, limitations: "requires the physical board"}
      - {id: qemu-user, method: simulation, command: "qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu ./build/bench_ringbuf.aarch64 --p99-max-us 2", requires: {tools: [qemu-aarch64]}, limitations: "QEMU timing is not representative of the SoC; at most partial evidence for R3"}
constraints:
  - {id: C1, kind: HARD, statement: "ISR latency must be measured on the real board; simulation cannot close R3.", protects: [R3]}
  - {id: C2, kind: ASSUMPTION, statement: "A board is needed before any testing can start (to be challenged)."}
  - {id: C3, kind: NEGOTIABLE, statement: "Choice of cross toolchain (gcc/zig/clang) is free."}
environment_assumptions:
  - {id: A1, statement: "An ARM64 board is reachable", probe: {env: [RVD_ARM_BOARD_SSH]}}
risk_policy: {remote_execution: ask, network: ask, paid_resources: deny, production: deny}
budget: {max_consecutive_no_progress: 2}
completion_policy: {require_all_mandatory: true, unreferenced_tasks: allow}

last_assistant_message:
The ring buffer isn't finished. R1 and R2 pass, but R3, the latency requirement on the board, is blocked and I can't close it from here.

| Requirement | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R1: push/pop/full/empty/wrap-around | Pass | `test_ringbuf` passes on the host (`host-cc` check) |
| R2: compiles for aarch64 | Pass | `clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu` builds `build/ringbuf.aarch64.o`, and `tools/check_elf.py` confirms it is an AArch64 ELF (e_machine=183) |
| R3: `rb_push`+`rb_pop` p99 < 2µs on the board | Blocked | Not run |

**Why R3 is blocked**
- `RVD_ARM_BOARD_SSH` isn't set and `ssh` isn't installed here, so I have no route to the board.
- `qemu-aarch64` isn't installed either. That wouldn't close R3 anyway. Your constraint C1 says latency has to be measured on the real board, and QEMU timing isn't representative of the SoC.
- `bench_ringbuf` doesn't exist in the repo yet. The board check runs `./bench_ringbuf --p99-max-us 2`, so that program has to be written and put on the board.

I haven't edited the goal or lowered the bar for R3. I also haven't made any claim about latency, because nothing has measured it. Reading the code, `% RB_CAP` is cheap with a power-of-two capacity of 8, so I'd expect it to pass, but that's a guess.

**What I need from you**
1. The board's SSH target, set as `RVD_ARM_BOARD_SSH` in this environment, with `ssh` available. Running on the board is a remote execution, which your policy marks as "ask", so I'll confirm with you before the first run.
2. Agreement that I write `bench_ringbuf.c` now. It would time `rb_push`+`rb_pop` with the ARM64 cycle counter (`cntvct_el0`), report p99, and exit non-zero if p99 is over the limit. I'd cross-compile it with clang and copy it to the board once access exists.

If you can't get board access, say so, and I'll file an amendment proposal with `rvd amend propose` instead of working around the requirement.
